notesDetails.title: Reactive System-Message Waiting vs. Busy-Polling: Only 7 manage_task Calls Across 11 Backgrounded Tasks (vs. 105 Polls on gemini-3.8-flash-high)
bullets: 93% Reduction in `manage_task` Polling Turns: Whenever a `run_command` exceeded the 10-second synchronous wait threshold (`WaitMsBeforeAsync: 10000`), Antigravity CLI backgrounded the command (`11` times total: `task-225`, `task-242`, `task-276`, `task-301`, `task-325`, `task-331`, `task-378`, `task-383`, `task-388`, `task-417`, and `task-428`) and logged `root agent idle; waiting for 1 background task(s) to finish` on `stderr.log` until emitting a `system_message` wakeup.

Waiting for Reactive Wakeups Instead of Looping: Unlike the earlier `antigravity cli` run on `gemini-3.8-flash-high`—which burned `105` `manage_task` calls (`27.1%` of all turns and `$1.68` / `31%` of total cost) polling every `3.5s`—`gemini-4-carbon` ended its turn immediately and waited for the harness's `system_message` wakeup on most backgrounded test suites (`S3` Steps `225–228` & `242–245`, `S4` Steps `276–280`, `S5` Steps `301–303`, and `S6` Steps `325–327`), invoking `manage_task(Action: "list")` only `7` times across the entire run (`3.0%` of tool calls).

Harness Comparison (`antigravity cli` vs. `omp` on `gemini-4-carbon` High): Against `omp` running the same `gemini-4-carbon` (`High`) model, `antigravity cli` used `7.5%` fewer LLM turns (`198` vs. `214`) and `8.7%` fewer tool calls (`231` vs. `253`), while costing `$7.16` vs. `$5.91` (`+21.2%`) due to `5` mid-run prefix cache evictions (`94.68%` vs. `96.74%` cache hit rate) and a `2.07x` larger initial system/tool schema prompt (`13,114` vs. `6,339` tokens across `58` registered tools vs. `4`).

notesDetails.title: Two-File Startup Handshake (CB_INTR_FILE + CB_READY_FILE) Solved the 20 ms–220 ms BEAM Boot-Window Ctrl-C Race During Release Verification
bullets: Upfront OTP 28 Bytecode Decompilation in `Preparation` (Steps `15–38`): Before writing `S1`, the agent decompiled `:erl_signal_handler` and `:pubkey_os_cacerts` abstract code via `:beam_lib.chunks/2`, verifying that `+Bi` prevents BEAM's break menu on `SIGINT` while `:os.set_signal(:sigusr2, :handle)` routes `SIGUSR2` cleanly to `:erl_signal_server`.

Catching the `50 ms–220 ms` Early-Boot `Ctrl-C` Race in Release Verification (Steps `392–426`): After finishing `S7` at Step `381`, the agent ran a standalone Python PTY sweep sending `\x03` at `50 ms`, `150 ms`, `220 ms`, `300 ms`, and `550 ms` (Steps `392` and `406`). It discovered that when `Ctrl-C` arrived during the first `~220 ms` of BEAM startup—before Elixir finished booting `CapyBench.CLI.main/1` and registering `:os.set_signal(:sigusr2, :handle)`—either `kill -USR2` killed the VM with default `SIGUSR2` disposition (`User defined signal 2: 31`) or the interrupt was lost before the handler was installed, producing empty `stdout` (`out=b''`).

Zero-Race `CB_INTR_FILE` + `CB_READY_FILE` Fix: In Steps `402–426`, the agent upgraded `./cb` and `CapyBench.CLI` with a two-file handshake (`CB_INTR_FILE` and `CB_READY_FILE`): `./cb`'s `INT` trap always touches `"$intr_file"` (`: > "$intr_file"`) and only sends `kill -USR2 "$pid"` if `"$ready_file"` already exists; once `CapyBench.Signal.install/1` registers `:sigusr2`, `CapyBench.CLI` touches `CB_READY_FILE` and immediately checks `File.exists?(intr_file)` to self-trigger `on_interrupt.()`. It also replaced `wait "$pid"` with a `while :; do wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null ...` loop so `/bin/sh` never prints `User defined signal 2` job notifications or exits before the partial summary flushes.

Following the `19m 57s` stream interruption at Step `211`, the prefix cache evicted (`cache_read_tokens: 0`) `5` times—at Step `213` (`118,881` tokens), Step `252` (`152,730`), Step `268` (`158,854`), Step `349` (`215,586`), and Step `355` (`220,037`)—re-billing `866,088` prompt tokens at full uncached rates (`$1.65` in extra input cost).

Active Inference vs. Tool Execution Split & Parallel Tool Batching: Excluding the `1,196.8s` stream stall at Step `211`, LLM generation accounted for `4,626.6s` (`77m 06.6s`, `87.2%` of active run time, avg `23.49s/turn`) while all `231` tool calls (with `27` multi-tool turns batching up to `4` parallel tool calls, `1.17` tools/turn) and backgrounded `mix test` runs completed in `680.0s` (`11m 20.0s`, `12.8%` of active time).
